mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level, currently at 0.37%, is a persistent driver of equity valuation. Lower rates compress discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of the 20-day periods following a month with FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings slowdowns and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The interaction effect is stronger than the sum of individual effects.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS and HOUST both rise by more than 0.5% in the past month, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over the past three months signals higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 1.1 million units per month are a persistent driver of positive equity returns, as they signal robust consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST is above 1.1 million units, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.0 over the past month signals weakening economic activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods when INDPRO falls below 102.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and economic momentum, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The interaction effect is stronger than the sum of individual effects.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 0.5% and HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS and HOUST both rise by more than 0.5% in the past month, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by low unemployment and strong job growth), a rising unemployment rate signals the beginning of a slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: In periods meeting the late-cycle expansion regime (UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS rise > 0.3% in 1 month), a rise in UNRATE leads to positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.
